---
title: "If so, how far?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

The glide that follows from the built glider's own trim, set against the design's,
from the same release height.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified
**All-up mass 16 g, balance point 15 mm aft of the plan's** · measured on the
built glider by the user, 2026-08-30.

**Release height 1.5 m** · as for the design, so the two are comparable.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed
Still air, and a glide already settled at trim. More seriously, the built
glider's trim lies past the stall, where `AeroBuildup` is reading NeuralFoil
beyond the attached-flow regime it represents well. The range below is what the
model says, not what the model can support.
:::

```{python}
H, BUILT_M, SHIFT = 1.5, 0.016, 0.015

x_np = neutral_point()
x_cg_plan = x_np - 0.10 * c_w
plan = trim(0.01550, x_cg_plan)
built = trim(BUILT_M, x_cg_built := x_cg_plan + SHIFT)
a_stall, _ = stall(built["V"])
```

**Answer.** The model says `{python} f"{built['LD']*H:.1f}"` m, against
`{python} f"{plan['LD']*H:.1f}"` m for the design — a glide ratio of
`{python} f"{built['LD']:.2f}"` where the plan gives
`{python} f"{plan['LD']:.2f}"`, so about
`{python} f"{(1 - built['LD']/plan['LD'])*100:.0f}"`% less distance for the same
release. It also comes down faster, sinking
`{python} f"{built['sink']:.2f}"` m/s against
`{python} f"{plan['sink']:.2f}"`, so it is airborne
`{python} f"{H/built['sink']:.1f}"` s instead of
`{python} f"{H/plan['sink']:.1f}"`.

**Do not trust that number.** It is computed at
`{python} f"{built['alpha']:.1f}"`°, and the wing stalls at
`{python} f"{a_stall:.1f}"`°, so the aircraft is trimmed past the point where
the flow stays attached. The section data behind it is a smooth NACA
approximation to a flat plate, which is optimistic before the stall and
unreliable after it. Read
`{python} f"{built['LD']*H:.1f}"` m as an upper bound on a flight that will
really be a nose-high mush, and expect a real glider to land nearer the thrower
than that — with the direction it lands in largely decided by which wing drops
first.

The useful comparison is not the two distances but their cause: the design flies
`{python} f"{stall(plan['V'])[0]-plan['alpha']:.1f}"`° below the stall and the
article flies past it. Recovering the distance is not a matter of trimming for
range; it is a matter of moving the balance point forward until the aircraft is
flying on the right side of its own polar again.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-range
#| tbl-cap: "Glide from a 1.5 m release, each at its own trim. The built column is quoted for completeness, not for confidence."
import pandas as pd

pd.DataFrame({
    "": ["trims at", "trim speed", "lift coefficient", "glide ratio",
         "sink rate", "range from 1.5 m", "time aloft"],
    "as planned": [f"{plan['alpha']:.1f}°", f"{plan['V']:.2f} m/s",
                   f"{plan['CL']:.3f}", f"{plan['LD']:.2f} : 1",
                   f"{plan['sink']:.2f} m/s", f"{plan['LD']*H:.1f} m",
                   f"{H/plan['sink']:.1f} s"],
    "as built": [f"{built['alpha']:.1f}°", f"{built['V']:.2f} m/s",
                 f"{built['CL']:.3f}", f"{built['LD']:.2f} : 1",
                 f"{built['sink']:.2f} m/s", f"{built['LD']*H:.1f} m",
                 f"{H/built['sink']:.1f} s"],
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```
